intro: A martial art's name can be claimed by many hands at once. A nation may list it as heritage or name it a national sport. A world federation may register its initials and run its championships. A founder's heirs may each say they carry the true line. A school far from the art's birthplace may answer to all of them, or to none.

Memory works the same way. Gyms hang photographs, name holidays and carve stones, and each choice leaves someone out. Many arts grew up under empire, occupation and slavery. Okinawa was annexed, Korea was colonized, and capoeira came from enslaved Africans in Brazil. Boxing rules changed after deaths in the ring.

In this unit you will weigh claims with dated records: treaties, laws, lectures, court cases and certificates. You will be able to explain who backs each claim to a name and why. You will also be able to describe hard history plainly, with dates and consequences.
bigQuestion: Who has the right to claim and remember a martial art, and what records should decide it?

timeline.t: Zumbi, last leader of Palmares, is killed in Brazil
Kanō Jigorō lectures in Tokyo on judo's three aims
Jack Johnson wins the heavyweight title; the Kasato Maru reaches Brazil
Okinawan teachers meet in Naha on October 25
Hwang Kee founds the Moo Duk Kwan in Seoul
Choi Hong-hi founds the International Taekwon-Do Federation
Duk Koo Kim dies after a title bout; title fights shrink to 12 rounds
Akebono becomes the first foreign-born yokozuna
UNESCO adopts its intangible cultural heritage convention
Korea names taekwondo its national sport; Jack Johnson is pardoned
The IOC withdraws recognition of the IBA

words.d: living practices that communities pass on and that UNESCO's 2003 convention aims to protect
one who cares for something on behalf of others without owning it outright
the image a country builds for itself abroad through culture and sport
an association of national bodies that writes shared rules and runs world events
for the IOC, to accept a federation officially as the world body for a sport
a split of one organization into rival groups
the process of choosing who takes over after a leader dies or leaves
people or institutions spread far from their homeland who keep ties to it
a record made at the time by someone involved
an act, such as a holiday or monument, that honors a past event
the study of how history has been written, and why
happening after a person has died

test.q: What does a UNESCO heritage listing give a state?
choices: A role as submitter and steward, not ownership
The right to ban other countries
test.why: The 2003 convention lists bearers and a safeguarding plan; it grants no ownership.

test.q: Which two states jointly nominated ssireum in 2018?
test.why: The ssireum listing was the first joint listing by the two Koreas.

test.q: What did Cambodia name the ring event it hosted at the 2023 Southeast Asian Games?
test.why: As host, Cambodia called the event Kun Khmer.

test.q: Which world body became World Taekwondo in 2017?
test.why: The World Taekwondo Federation shortened its name in June 2017.

test.q: Who ran Olympic boxing at Paris 2024?
test.why: After suspending the federation, the IOC organized boxing itself.

test.q: Which aikido group was founded in 1974?
test.why: Tōhei Kōichi founded the Ki Society in 1974.

test.q: What happened to Kyokushin after its founder died in 1994?
choices: It split into rival groups using the name
test.why: No successor was accepted by all, so several groups claimed the name.

test.q: Why is Kanō's 1889 lecture strong evidence about judo's aims?
choices: It was written after his death
It was made for a film
It is a dated primary source that was printed
test.why: A printed lecture from the time lets readers check what the founder said.

test.q: Who founded the Moo Duk Kwan and kept the name Tang Soo Do?
test.why: Hwang Kee founded the Moo Duk Kwan in 1945 and stayed out of the taekwondo merger.

test.q: What did Moenig's study argue about taekwondo's early roots?
choices: They lay only in the hwarang
They lay largely in karate learned under Japanese rule
test.why: Moenig traced early taekwondo to karate learned during the colonial period.

test.q: Why did many activists choose November 20 to honor Afro-Brazilian history?
choices: It marks the first capoeira academy
It is the day Zumbi of Palmares was killed in 1695
test.why: The date honors Zumbi's resistance rather than a royal decree.
President Trump granted a posthumous pardon on May 24, 2018.

test.q: Why did the length of boxing title fights change in the 1980s?
choices: After Duk Koo Kim died following a 1982 bout
test.why: Kim's death led the WBC to cut title fights from 15 to 12 rounds.

test.q: Which rule did the Japan Sumo Association tighten in 2010?
choices: A limit of one foreign-born wrestler per stable, now counting naturalized citizens
A rule that yokozuna must be from Tokyo
test.why: The 2010 change counted naturalized citizens under the one-per-stable limit.

test.q: What did the 2018 taekwondo demonstrations in Korea show?
choices: That the ITF and World Taekwondo had merged
That taekwondo was dropped from the Olympics
That two divided federations could share a stage
test.why: Teams from both federations performed together without merging.

write.prompt: Who should have the strongest claim to a martial art's name: a nation, a world federation or a founder's students? Argue from at least three dated records in this unit, such as the 2003 UNESCO convention, the 2018 Korean law, Kanō's 1889 lecture or the 2023 IOC decision.
tips: Name each record and give its date.
Say which institution stands behind each claim.
Attribute beliefs to the group that holds them.
Compare claims rather than judging a people or a tradition.
Use unit terms such as steward, recognize and succession.
